headline: Software Leads a Broad Rally as Geopolitical Fog Keeps Energy in Check
body_html:
Thursday's session ended on a constructive note, with advancing issues outpacing decliners by a margin of 344 to 197 across the 545-name universe — a breadth reading that pointed to genuine participation rather than a narrow, index-driven lift. Software led all sectors with a gain of 1.58%, followed by Industrials at 1.03% and Homebuilders at 0.59%, while Semiconductors and Consumer names edged fractionally higher. The day's character was one of selective risk appetite: investors reached for growth and domestic-demand stories while treating commodity-linked names with caution.

The session's dominant headwind came from the Middle East. Diesel prices hit record levels as intensifying conflict squeezed supply chains, and crude itself traded in choppy, mixed fashion as markets weighed escalation risk against the possibility of a Russia-Ukraine diplomatic opening. Energy closed down 0.57% and Materials shed 0.60%, with offshore-vessel operator Tidewater falling nearly 6% and metallurgical-coal producer Alpha Metallurgical dropping almost 7%.

The standout mover of the day was Snowflake, which surged more than 16% — the sharpest single-session advance in the universe — on what appeared to be renewed conviction that the data-cloud platform has navigated artificial-intelligence disruption concerns. Where energy stumbled, software sprinted; Thursday offered a clean illustration of how geopolitical uncertainty can simultaneously punish one corner of the market while handing another a tailwind.

briefs.headline: Snowflake Rockets 16%-Plus, Anchors Software's Surge
briefs.body: Snowflake posted a gain of more than 16.5% on Thursday, the largest advance in the universe, as investors appeared to set aside lingering worries about AI-driven disruption to data-cloud platforms. Twilio added 6.1% and CrowdStrike climbed 5.7%, giving the Software sector a 1.58% close — the day's top-performing group by a wide margin.

briefs.headline: Diesel Hits Record as Middle East Conflict Tightens Supply
briefs.body: U.S. diesel prices reached a record high Thursday, according to Reuters, as ongoing Middle East hostilities further strained an already tight fuel-supply picture. The development weighed on sentiment in commodity-linked sectors, with Energy closing down 0.57% even as crude oil itself traded in mixed fashion amid competing geopolitical signals.

briefs.headline: Victoria's Secret Tumbles More Than 13%, Leads Decliners
briefs.body: Victoria's Secret was the session's worst performer, shedding 13.2% to sit well clear of the next decliner on the list. The consumer-apparel name offered no company-specific catalyst in Thursday's news flow, suggesting the move may have reflected broader rotation away from discretionary retail as investors favored technology over consumption-facing names.

briefs.headline: Vance Sidesteps Timeline on Iran Conflict, Probes Airstrike Report
briefs.body: Vice President Vance declined Thursday to characterize the ongoing U.S.-Iran situation as a war or provide any end-date guidance, according to Reuters. Separately, the administration said it is examining an airstrike that Iranian officials claim struck a wedding gathering, adding a fresh layer of diplomatic sensitivity to an already fraught standoff.

briefs.headline: Ciena and Sprinklr Each Drop More Than 10%
briefs.body: Optical-networking specialist Ciena fell 10.4% and customer-experience software firm Sprinklr declined 10.2%, making the pair the second- and third-largest losers on Thursday. Both moves came without prominent company-specific headlines, pointing to either technical selling or portfolio repositioning as the session's risk-on tilt concentrated gains in higher-growth software names.

briefs.headline: Automakers Press Congress to Permanently Bar Chinese Connected Vehicles
briefs.body: Major auto manufacturers urged U.S. lawmakers Thursday to make permanent a ban on Chinese-made connected vehicles in the American market, escalating an industry push that has gained momentum alongside broader trade-security concerns. The appeal comes as Washington continues to tighten scrutiny of foreign-linked technology embedded in consumer and commercial transportation.
